analytic.title: Application of Classic Rating-Monotonic Scheduling Algorithm in UAV Engine Test System

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Modern unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) engine testing has a wide range of high real-time requirements. Previous research based on non-real-time was unable to meet these test requirements. This paper integrate classic rate monotonic (RM) with the software systems for UAV engine test platform to satisfy the requirements. Besides, this paper analyzes the criterion of the classical RM algorithm schedulability and describes the design process of task set. The testing for the real schedulability of the tasks shows that the desired effect of system is achieved and the maximum hardware utilization reaches 93.8%, which meets the design requirements.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) Engine test system has a wide range of project, high real-time requirements and the strict stability, etc. Compared with ordinary engine testing, UAV engine testing complies with higher testing requirements. In the early design, a small system on a chip is the core of the measure and control system, in which the program operates with non-real time sequential structure and the task is executed in serial mode [1][2][3]. Many systems use this program design because of its simple structure and easy realization. But with the increasing complexity of system, the design does not perform very well. As many countries attach importance to UAV, there are more and more advanced UAV engine test systems. Haigang Xie, et al. proposed a design method of control system based on Real-Time Operating System (RTOS), which combines the engine control system with the real-time operating system to verify the engine test [4]. Yuehua Ma, et al. proposed that in order to achieve high-speed data acquisition, they try to use multi-threading technology and multi-level cache technology in the test system [5]. On their research, Yong he et al. presented a novel design method of data acquisition system to enhance the measurement accuracy and stability of the system, which regards VXI data acquisition equipment as the core [6]. Although those researches have realized different test bench designs of different types of aircraft engine, none of them discuss the scheduling problem of engine test system in detail.

When facing complex tasks, the specific scheduling strategy has been discussed in other areas [7,8], yet, there are few engineering verification in the UAV engine test field. In this paper, we aim at the task scheduling and resource allocation in measure and control hardware system. This research includes task design method, judgments of scheduling and measuring method.

div.head: II. RM SCHEDULING ALGORITHM
div.p: Rate monotonic (RM) algorithm, proposed by Liu and Layland in 1973, is an optimal static priority scheduling algorithm which is suitable to achieve preemption in real-time periodic task scheduling [9]. The basic idea of RM scheduling is that if the execution cycle of one task is shorter, it will obtain priority to execute its task and preempt other tasks' execution time [10].

According to the table, execution time is the worst-case execution time C i so the execution time isn't longer than C i even if the task is executed in the worst condition. Because periodicity represents time characteristics of triggered tasks, we can set periodic table of the tasks to achieve the best use of CPU based on the real-time requirement. If task is triggered in random and occasionally, it is regarded as sporadic task and there is not specific regulation. What must be met in the system is the real-time requirement which is the worst constraints of task.

div.head: B. Sporadic Task
div.p: Sporadic task is the response for an event in the system which is released irregularly, so there is not periodic relationship between sporadic task and other events. But sporadic task must have a maximum release rate. In other words, there must be a minimum time interval between these recurring successful releases of sporadic tasks to meet the time limit to complete tasks. In a certain engine test measure and control system, sporadic tasks include response task of console and the task of data communication.

div.head: C. Release and Scheduling of Data Communication
div.p: There are two situations about the RM scheduling of data communication task: 1) As shown in Fig. 3-a, the tasks of t 3 and t 4 , such as the tasks of transmission control unit (TCU) and cylinder temperature, can be executed in a process period and later the data communication can be released. 2) As shown in Fig. 3-b, the tasks of t 3 and t 4 are executed in two different process periods and the data communication is released after both of them are executed. As shown in Fig. 3, there are also two situations of the task t 2 execution and in order to meet the requirement of data transmission, its execution period (T 2 ) should satisfy the requirement:

div.head: V. CONCLUSION
div.p: This paper presents the process of RM scheduling of the task set including the sporadic tasks and non-independent tasks. Sporadic task is regarded as a specific time in a scheduling period. When the sporadic task is released during the scheduling period, it can be executed in this period, otherwise, it would be switched to other tasks and executed in other periods. Because the release of non-independent task depends on the fulfillment of other tasks, non-independent task is regarded as an independent periodic task of which period is the minimum interval of time to achieve the judgment of RM schedulability.
